summary: This House resolution calls on all Americans to observe Memorial Day 2026 by honoring U.S. Armed Forces members who died in service to freedom and peace, as an expression of respect and gratitude.

scores.thoughts: This is a purely symbolic House resolution calling for Americans to honor fallen Armed Forces members on Memorial Day. It contains no provisions, authorizations, or directives related to federal budgets, appropriations, or spending levels of any kind.
The resolution is commemorative and makes no reference to tax policy, rates, credits, or revenue measures.
No content in the bill addresses healthcare systems, coverage, funding, or regulation.
The bill does not mention firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions or language concerning immigration policy, borders, or pathways to citizenship.
The resolution contains no language related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
While the resolution honors members of the Armed Forces, it does not address defense budgets, military spending levels, procurement, or force structure. It is strictly commemorative.
No engagement with environmental regulations, climate policy, or conservation measures.
The bill makes no reference to welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety net policies.
No provisions related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
The resolution does not address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance policy.
No content concerning sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill contains nothing related to tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
No discussion of deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
The resolution does not address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions or statements concerning foreign assistance or international aid.
The bill makes no reference to voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No engagement with technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The resolution does not address worker protections, union rights, or labor policy.
No language concerning religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination policy.
